corrections.form_value: Hedges' g: standardized mean difference between the human-AI collaboration condition and the human-only condition, converted from reported means, SDs, t-values; mixed creativity indicators (originality, fluency, flexibility, appropriateness, elaboration, global creativity, other) and rater types (layperson, expert, self-report, machine); paired designs use an assumed pre-post correlation
corrections.source_says: Specify the different denominators documented in the later supplement. Posttest-only effects divide the experimental-control mean difference by the sample-size-weighted pooled SD. Controlled pretest-posttest effects divide the between-group difference in mean improvement by the weighted pooled pretest SD. The paired-design formula divides the condition mean difference by sqrt(SD_exp^2 + SD_ctrl^2 - 2*r*SD_exp*SD_ctrl), the SD of the difference scores. Cohen's d is then multiplied by the Hedges correction J. These pooled g values therefore combine different standardization bases; this detail extends the v2 main text and must be attributed to the separately read supplement.
corrections.quote: For a pretest–posttest design, the effect size was computed by dividing the difference of mean improvement between the training group and the control group by their weighted pooled pretest standard deviation

No local markdown/PDF is listed for c138 in retrieval.json. Main PDF: https://osf.io/download/m42jh/; supplement: https://osf.io/download/nh53g/.

The main source is PsyArXiv jy3ba_v2, published 2026-01-21, with the title variants and author list recorded in the form (OSF preprint API date_published/version/primary_file; main PDF pp. 1 and 4). The v1 API record is dated 2025-08-06 and reports 44 studies, 141 effects, and g = 0.54; even the v2 API description retains those older numbers, whereas the v2 PDF gives the larger analysis.

Design_class = synthesis, context_class = synthesis, and core = no are correct. The paper synthesizes other studies and reports no original randomized experiment with people; its included trials do not make this paper a new randomized people study (main PDF pp. 18-25, Method and Data Analysis).

Counts are 67 articles, 115 independent studies, and 322 effect sizes, not 115 or 322 participants; 86% were published in peer-reviewed journals (main PDF p. 7, Results; p. 19, Literature search). The main PDF does not state a unique total of people randomized or analyzed, so null participant counts are appropriate.

The search covers publications from 2020 through October 31, 2025. Random assignment is not required by the inclusion criteria; independent and paired designs are included, and random assignment is one of four quality indicators (main PDF p. 19, Literature search; pp. 24-25, Sensitivity analysis by study design and Study quality assessment).
The one-line finding and overall pooled entry match: g = 0.62, SE = 0.08, t(321) = 7.70, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.46, 0.78] (main PDF p. 7, Overall analysis; p. 4, Abstract; p. 37, Fig. 2).
The adjusted entry matches the study-clustered PEESE result: g = 0.25, SE = 0.06, t(113) = 3.95, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.12, 0.37] (main PDF p. 23, Bias tests; also pp. 4 and 8).

The higher-quality subset is 36 studies and 88 effect sizes, meeting at least three of pre-test, control group, random assignment, and power analysis; g = 0.74, SE = 0.17, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.41, 1.08] (main PDF p. 25, Study quality assessment).

Excluding samples with fewer than 30 participants leaves 100 studies and 282 effect sizes; g = 0.55, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.40, 0.71]. This is the review's sensitivity threshold, not an Atlas count of people in a primary experiment (main PDF p. 24, Small sample exclusion).

Residual-outlier exclusions match: articles, 296 effects, g = 0.49, CI [0.37, 0.60]; studies, 306 effects, g = 0.52, CI [0.39, 0.64]; effects, 315 effects, g = 0.59, CI [0.45, 0.73]. All are 95% intervals; the Cook's-distance range is g = 0.64 to 0.65 (main PDF p. 24, Outlier diagnostics and exclusion).

Paired-correlation sensitivities match: r = 0.3, g = 0.61, SE = 0.08, 95% CI [0.46, 0.77]; r = 0.5, g = 0.62, SE = 0.08, 95% CI [0.46, 0.78]; r = 0.7, g = 0.64, SE = 0.09, 95% CI [0.47, 0.81] (main PDF pp. 24-25, Sensitivity analysis by study design).

The atypical-population analysis covers two investigations and 10 effect sizes, excluded from the main analysis: g = 0.64, SE = 0.18, t(9) = 3.51, p = 0.007, 95% CI [0.23, 1.05] (main PDF p. 10, Exploratory analysis).

The form correctly identifies mixed creativity dimensions, text/image/multimodal tasks, real-time and training uses, and self-report among rater types; these pooled effects do not isolate the Atlas's randomized output-scored population (main PDF pp. 9-10 and Tables 1-2, pp. 33-35; supplement S2.9, PDF p. 29, explicitly lists randomized, quasi-experimental, and cross-sectional designs).

PROSPERO registration CRD42024618486, the separate supplementary-material references, the academic affiliations, the stated public funding, and Declaration of Competing Interest: None are consistent with the form (main PDF pp. 1-2 and 18).
summary: The v2 manuscript is a synthesis with no original randomized people study, and its study counts and reported pooled estimates match the form. Four corrections address omitted data/code links, incomplete standardizer details, the available supplement and its protocol-deviation locator, and Cook's-distance intervals supplied by that later supplement.
